claim_support.claim: SAM uses a normalized current gradient to approximate the Euclidean perturbation inner step.
claim_support.evidence: Section 2, first-order inner maximization and Algorithm 1.

claim_support.claim: ASAM adapts the perturbation region to parameter scale through a normalization operator.
claim_support.evidence: Sections 3-4 define the transformed neighborhood and corresponding perturbation.

claim_support.claim: SSAM masks the SAM perturbation using Fisher-based or dynamically updated sparse masks.
claim_support.evidence: Section 4.1 masks the already normalized perturbation; Sections 4.2-4.3 define mask construction.

claim_support.claim: The preSAM framework separates objective preconditioning from constraint preconditioning.
claim_support.evidence: Section III-A, equations 4-5, and Section III-C; objective preconditioning includes D=I.

claim_support.claim: GEAR-SAM uses an EMA of squared block-gradient norms to allocate a fixed global perturbation budget.
claim_support.evidence: Section III-C equations 16-17; Section III-D constrains squared block radii to the global budget.

claim_support.claim: CrAM incorporates a compression operator into training to prepare dense models for one-shot compression.
claim_support.evidence: Section 3.1 equations 1-2; Section 4 also evaluates semi-structured sparsity.

claim_support.claim: AdaSAP adapts neuron perturbations before channel pruning and subsequently trains for robustness.
claim_support.evidence: Section 3 describes three stages; Section 3.1 gives importance-dependent neuron radii.

claim_support.claim: OBC uses ExactOBS for layerwise post-training pruning and extends the procedure to N:M sparsity.
claim_support.evidence: Sections 3-4 define quadratic layer reconstruction, inverse-Hessian compensation and the N:M extension.

claim_support.claim: SparseGPT performs approximate second-order layer reconstruction for one-shot pruning, including 2:4 and 4:8 patterns.
claim_support.evidence: Sections 3.1-3.3; the official ICML abstract explicitly identifies both semi-structured patterns.

claim_support.claim: ROSE changes column and block processing order within the SparseGPT pruning workflow.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract and Section 4.2 describe two-level reordering based on estimated pruning losses.

claim_support.claim: SR-STE trains N:M sparse networks from scratch using a sparse-refined straight-through estimator.
claim_support.evidence: Official abstract identifies the training setting and the SR-STE estimator.

claim_support.claim: Wanda prunes per-output weights using magnitude multiplied by the corresponding input activation scale, without a compensating weight update.
claim_support.evidence: Official abstract states magnitude times input activations and no retraining or weight update.
